studies.headline: Coracias garrulus occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: -0.065 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.575 in 1987-1991 against 0.510 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.058 and 0.048.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.542 to 0.452 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window
rows.detail: 2019-2023 in place of 2008-2012, and the sign agrees

studies.headline: Canis lupus is in this project's data, and none of it is drawn.
studies.detail: 68 animals, 2000-2011, classified high.
studies.caveat: The one demonstrated pathway in the literature. An anti-wolf site published instructions for locating collared wolves by telemetry; Idaho subsequently made telemetry-aided hunting specifically illegal; four of the eleven collared wolves on Yellowstone's Northern Range were shot in a single season. Alberta runs wolf culls. Cooke et al. 2017, Conservation Biology, cobi.12895.
